name: eBay ex-datacenter A100 rack liquidation (32x A100 40GB compute-node rack, repeated lots)
region: United States (Minneapolis, MN; free local pickup within 60 mi)
price_basis: USED, WHOLE RACK: 4 compute nodes x 8 GPUs = 32x NVIDIA A100 40GB per rack, including the servers/chassis - NOT bare cards. $249,000.00 or Best Offer per rack, captured 2026-10-03. Implied $7,781 per GPU, versus ~$2,500 for a bare used 40GB SXM4 module and ~$3,000-$4,000 for the same GPU with its host server in other listings - i.e. the rack premium is the node/host cost, not GPU scarcity. Warranty: none. Seller does not accept returns.
notes: ACCELERATOR-ID CORRECTION (2026-10-03, parent agent): this record's price_basis states 4 nodes x 8 = 32x A100 **40GB**, but accelerator_ids read nvidia-a100-80gb-sxm4. Corrected to the 40GB part; no 40GB SXM4 accelerator record existed at the time so the mislabel was the only option. The 80GB and 40GB parts differ ~2x in price and capacity, so the mislabel was material. The clearest real-world example of the ex-datacenter liquidation pattern. Quantity 'More than 10 available' makes this a REPEATED-LOT channel, not a one-of-a-kind - so the $249,000 figure is a repeatable market price, not an auction artefact. Free FedEx Ground; seller will not accept returns, which is the norm for liquidation lots and means you absorb all DOA risk. Seller 20,700 feedback. HOW TO READ THE NUMBER: at $7,781/GPU the rack is roughly 3x the bare-module price, so this is the route to buy A100s WITH servers, not a cheap route to A100s. It only makes sense if you need integrated nodes. Same seller's adjacent listings show the same structure at other scales: 8x40GB HGX baseboard $70,170.51 (~$8,771/GPU), 8x80GB HGX baseboard $213,039.54 (~$26,630/GPU), 8x80GB HGX GDX H100 baseboard $341,872.75 (~$42,734/GPU), HPE server with 8x V100 SXM2 NVLink ring at $18,000 pre-owned (~$2,250/GPU). The V100 figure is the useful sanity check - ex-datacenter value tracks generation hard, and an 8-V100 server landing near bare-4090 territory is the floor of this market, not a special case.
